questions.problem:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.2$ $0.3$ $0.5$

$y$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.25$ $0.75$

Find $\text{Var}[3X+2Y].$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula 

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{X}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.2+2\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.5 \\  & =2.3\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.2+4\cdot 0.3+9\cdot 0.5 \\  & =5.9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5.9-{2.3}^{2} \\  & =0.61.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{Y}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =1\cdot 0.25+2\cdot 0.75 \\  & =1.75\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}{y}^{2}\cdot f(y) \\  & =1\cdot 0.25+4\cdot 0.75 \\  & =3.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =3.25-{1.75}^{2} \\  & =0.1875.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[3X-2Y] & ={3}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{2}^{2}\text{Var}[Y] \\  & ={3}^{2}(0.61)+{2}^{2}(0.1875) \\  & =6.24.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For two independent random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\text{Var}[X]=3$ and $\text{Var}[Y]=1.$ Find $\text{Var}[6X+4Y].$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent variables, and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain 

$$
\text{Var}[6X+4Y]={6}^{2}\cdot 3+{4}^{2}\cdot 1=124.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider two independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\text{E}[X]=8,$ $\text{E}[Y]=11$
and second raw moments $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=70$ and $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]=130.$ Find the variance of  $4X-\frac{1}{3}Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula 

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =70-{8}^{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =130-{11}^{2} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[4X-\frac{1}{3}Y] & ={4}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}\text{Var}[Y] \\  & =16\cdot 6+\frac{1}{9}\cdot 9 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$
